domain_analysis.scope: Interior new construction door slab stain and clear coat workflows
domain_analysis.workflow_overview: Three-layer coating system: stain (color) > sanding sealer (adhesion bridge + smooth base) > clear topcoat (protection + depth). EA-based per door slab. Door style modifiers drive significant rate variation. Sides dimension controls 1 or 2 face coverage.
key_differences_from_paint: Bare wood input (SS_BARE) instead of primed surface
No companion prime spec — stain spec handles all prep and coating layers
Three product roles (stain, sealer, clear) instead of one (finish)
Independent application method selection for stain vs clear phases
Wipe step mandatory for all stain application methods
Wood conditioner activation for softwood species
Grain raise management for waterborne products on bare wood
Door style modifiers adapted from paint spec complexity modifiers
No sheen/QT gate — all clear sheens available at all tiers
key_differences_from_trim_stain: EA-based (per door) instead of LF-based (per linear foot)
Door style modifiers instead of profile complexity modifiers
Sides dimension (1 or 2 faces) — unique to door spec
Fewer protection zones (floor_full + wall_adjacent vs floor_perimeter + wall_adjacent + fixture_covers)
Single paintable item (ITM_DOOR_SLAB) vs 7 trim types
Production rates expressed in minutes per EA instead of LF per hour

required_paintscope_keys.description: Count of door slabs to stain
Floor protection area under door work zone
Wall masking LF adjacent to door opening

zones.notes: Full drop cloths under door work area. Stain drips critical to catch.
Wall masking adjacent to door opening. Stain is difficult to remove from painted surfaces.

analysis.interface_concern: Door slab meets frame at reveal. Often same stain/clear finish.
analysis.protection_approach: No protection when same finish. Different finish requires masking at reveal line.

analysis.interface_concern: Door at opening. Stain harder to clean from painted walls.
analysis.protection_approach: Wall masking for spray or when walls finished.

state_analysis.notes: SS_STAINED and SS_CLEAR_COATED already registered by SF_TRIM_NC_STAIN (Tier 1 canonical spec).

key_rates.stain_brush_wipe_per_door: 30-45 min/EA — brush stain + wipe on one door slab (2 sides). Includes dwell + wipe time.
key_rates.stain_spray_wipe_per_door: 20-30 min/EA — spray stain + wipe. Faster application offset by wipe.
key_rates.clear_brush_per_door: 20-30 min/EA per coat — brush clear coat on one door slab.
key_rates.clear_spray_per_door: 15-20 min/EA per coat — spray clear coat.
key_rates.sealer_per_door: 15-20 min/EA per coat — thin sealer application.
key_rates.bare_wood_sand_per_door: 20-30 min/EA — sand both sides 120 then 150 grit.

door_style_modifiers.shaker: 1.25 — recessed panel, stain pooling in panel detail
door_style_modifiers.raised_panel: 1.35 — profiled faces, more wipe attention in detail

risk_notes.risk: Stain collects in recesses of panel and shaker style doors, creating uneven color
risk_notes.mitigation: Thorough wipe-out of panel details. Extra attention to inside corners. Apply thin coats.

risk_notes.risk: Door edges are visible when door is open. Uneven stain on edges is noticeable.
risk_notes.mitigation: Stain edges first, then faces. Consistent wipe technique on narrow edge surface.

risk_notes.topic: Clear coat runs on vertical door face
risk_notes.risk: Clear coat applied too heavily on vertical door face creates runs/sags
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin, even coats. Tip off with grain. Watch for runs at panel detail transitions.

assumptions.value: Doors may be stained on or off hinges. On-hinge is standard NC production (doors already hung). Off-hinge (on sawhorses) gives better access but requires more handling.
assumptions.note: Production rates assume on-hinge staining for brush method, either for spray.

assumptions.value: When sides=2, both faces receive same stain/clear treatment. Different stain colors per side is not supported in this spec.
assumptions.note: Two-tone stain doors are extremely rare in NC.
